arguments.context_notes: Webinar: Pricing for agencies, Thursday Dec 10 at 2pm New York time, free, sign up at acme.com/webinar. Week 1: why agencies underprice. Week 2: the countdown. Every post names the date, Thursday Dec 10, never 'in 3 days' or 'tomorrow', since posting days can move. Facts the user gave, nothing else.

steps.why: Problem / Solution (guidance): the pain the webinar solves, then the seat. Two weeks starting Friday Nov 27, so the second week ends on the event day, Thu Dec 10. X can't take a carousel, so the mix is text and an image, which both networks take. Accounts and notes go on the same create call, so it is made with them. Bolta spreads posts across the week, so a post saying "tomorrow" could land on the wrong day. Naming the date keeps every post true. A post that must say "today" is pinned to Dec 10 under Post prompts on the campaign page; no call does that.
The user said start and saw the plan. Week 1 starts Fri Nov 27, written around Wed Nov 25.
Read status active and schedule_status.state not needs_accounts before saying it is on.

say: Campaign on for Acme: Pricing for agencies webinar, Nov 27 to Dec 10 on LinkedIn and X, 2 text posts and 1 image a week, 6 drafts to review. Every post names Thursday Dec 10. Week 1's drafts land around Wed Nov 25. Want a "today, 2pm" post pinned to Dec 10? Add it under Post prompts at bolta.ai/dashboard/campaigns/<id>.
never: "3 days left" or "tomorrow" in notes for posts whose day isn't pinned.
Running the campaign past the event.
